decision.actionLabel: Tell the landlord what Flintmere still owes, and ask her to decide on a lockout diagnostic by Tuesday 21 October
decision.message:
Dear Nessa,

Thank you for your email of 17 October. Here is what Flintmere still owes us, and one decision we need from you.

Still outstanding from Flintmere:
1. The signed paperwork from the 9 October visit (job reference NBL-48217). The engineer recorded the check as satisfactory for the boiler and the cooker. On 14 October, however, Flintmere told us its quality desk has stopped issuing the signed paperwork while it checks "an appliance installation detail" against the details it holds for the address. They have not said which appliance this is about, what the detail is, or when the paperwork will be issued. The engineer has told us he cannot see or settle this query himself.
2. Because of that, our file still has no signed gas record from the 9 October visit. The only signed record we hold is dated 16 October 2024. The portal screenshot you sent us on 10 October shows the job as complete and satisfactory, but it also shows the customer document as "Processing", so it is not the signed paperwork.

We are emailing Flintmere today to ask for a firm issue date, what the installation query is about, and which appliance it affects.

Boiler lockouts – decision needed:
Iona has now told us about repeated lockouts: twice in the weekend before 1 October, overnight on 12–13 October, and again on the morning of 16 October. Each time the boiler restarted after she reset it, and she has not noticed a gas smell. The 9 October visit was a check only. Flintmere has confirmed that looking into the lockout would be a separate job, and nothing has been booked. We know you have not approved this or any other extra cost, and we will not instruct anything without your written approval.

Because this is a gas boiler that keeps locking out, please let us know by Tuesday 21 October whether you would like:
(a) us to ask Flintmere for a price for a lockout diagnostic. The price would come to you for approval before anything is booked.
(b) to arrange your own Gas Safe registered engineer. If so, please tell us who will contact Iona.
(c) something else.

Iona can give access from 21 October. If she reports a gas smell, a carbon monoxide alarm, or a lockout that will not reset, we will contact you straight away.

Kind regards,
Oren Vale
Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings
decision.rationale: The landlord asked a direct question on 17 October (E023) about what is still outstanding from Flintmere, and nobody has answered it. The landlord is the only person who can approve spend (E005, E016, E023), so she has to decide on the lockouts. Lockouts that reset with no gas smell are not an automatic escalation under the playbook. They are a risk inside a routine job, so the landlord gets the risk stated plainly and is asked for a prompt decision, and the tenant gets safety advice in the same turn. The one fact Flintmere has not given (an issue date and what the query is about, E019, E021, E024) goes to Flintmere as a separate chase. Flintmere's last message was 4.3 days ago and our question about timing is still open from E018. The tenant's questions from E014 and E022 have also gone unanswered and get a reply now. A person will take over if the landlord declines or stays silent past 21 October, or if any gas smell or CO alarm is reported.
decision.expectedOutcome: The landlord knows what is outstanding and replies by 21 October with a decision on the lockout. Flintmere gives an issue date and explains the installation query. The tenant knows where things stand and what to do if anything changes.
